Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Glyphic hornbook: heritable barcodes plus a pre-treatment transcriptional lookup table
ideas.description: Transduce cells with expressed DNA barcodes and split the population into one arm profiled by scRNA-seq before treatment and one arm treated, so each surviving clone's barcode can be looked up against the untreated 'hornbook' of states. This directly tests whether survivors arise from pre-existing, heritable transcriptional states rather than random chance, and identifies the specific priming programs.

ideas.title: Nitid/photolith: optical tagging of rare primed cells before drug exposure
ideas.description: Live-image a fluorescent reporter for a candidate priming marker and use photoconversion or photo-crosslinking to permanently mark the rare brightest cells, then sort and sequence them while following matched wells through treatment. This provides a causal link between a pre-drug optical phenotype and eventual survival, rather than a post hoc correlation.

ideas.title: Impute: sister-cell split assay to recover the survivor's pre-drug state
ideas.description: Physically separate sister cells right after mitosis, treat one sister with drug and molecularly profile the other, thereby imputing the pre-treatment state of the very cell that lived or died. Varying the interval between separation and treatment measures how long the predictive non-genetic memory persists.

ideas.title: Graduator/undo: fluctuation analysis plus reversibility kinetics
ideas.description: Perform Luria-Delbruck-style replicate expansions from small founder populations across a drug dose gradient to quantitatively partition survival into genetic, heritable-epigenetic, and transient non-genetic contributions. Then regrow survivor colonies without drug and re-challenge at increasing intervals to measure the timescale over which resistance is undone.

ideas.title: Innerve/embassy: spatial niche and paracrine messenger analysis
ideas.description: Apply spatial transcriptomics to 3D cultures or co-cultures to ask whether survivors occupy distinctive cellular neighborhoods, and pair this with conditioned-media transfer and ligand-trap or receptor-blockade perturbations. Together these distinguish cell-intrinsic survival states from protection delivered by secreted envoys from neighboring cells.
